extracted.intended_audience: government attorneys, military department officials, and practitioners advising on use, licensing, and disposition of public (military) property
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and principles governing revocable licenses, temporary uses, and disposition of property on U.S. military reservations, including the Secretary of War's authority, limits, required conditions, and related sale/condemnation procedures under section 1241 R.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of license
rubrics_metrics.description: A license is defined as a bare authority to do a certain act or series of acts upon the land of the licensor without possessing or acquiring any estate therein; it passes no interest in the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be created by parol though a writing defining exact nature and scope is preferable; it legalizes acts that would otherwise be trespasses but confers no estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War's power to grant revocable licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War may, by revocable license, permit a temporary use terminable at his discretion, provided such license conveys no usufructuary interest and such use does not conflict with the purpose for which the land is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority exercised subject to public interest, revocability, and non-conflict with military purposes; longstanding practice and precedent support such grants when beneficial to military service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit: license may not grant an interest (usurp authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument termed a revocable license but which in effect grants an interest (e.g., permanent improvement that becomes property of licensee) is in excess of executive authority and inoperative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: permits to erect permanent buildings to be used or disposed of by licensee or fixed-rental residence arrangements amounting to leases are invalid absent congressional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonassignability and scope limitation of licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A license does not justify any use other than as specified in the grant and therefore is not assignable; transfer of it avoids the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments have been held legally inoperative (e.g., assignment to erect a hotel on a military reservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: License does not authorize removal of public property
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to go upon U.S. land will not authorize the licensee to take public property therefrom (public property disposable only by Congress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Secretary not empowered to license gathering fruit from trees on Government land.

rubrics_metrics.name: No authority to license uses causing permanent injury or waste
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War is without authority to license the commission of waste upon military reservations or to permit uses which would permanently change or damage the reservation; such uses require congressional authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: applications to straighten a river boundary throwing acres out of a reservation or to take earth for brick manufacture are disallowed or doubtful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral/phosphate lands exception and prior valid claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of July 28, 1892, excepted 'mineral or phosphate lands' from leasing authority; such exception should be regarded as withholding authority to permit use of such lands under revocable license, except where a valid mining location predated the reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless, dredging for navigation that yields gold may be permitted; prior valid claims should be honored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on licensing religious buildings; statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary lacks authority to license construction of certain religious buildings on military reservations absent congressional authorization; Congress has granted limited authority (e.g., West Point by statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-1902 statutes authorized nonsectarian buildings for welfare (YMCA) and that may be applied to chapels for all denominations under certain circumstances; earlier Attorney General opinions denied authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major infrastructure incompatible with revocable license
rubrics_metrics.description: Large, permanent infrastructure (e.g., railway tunnels, sewer outlet tunnels) are inconsistent with the nature of a revocable license and are inappropriate uses to be authorized by license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such improvements are considered beyond the scope of temporary, revocable permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses must be conditioned to prevent permanent injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses granted to enter and use lands have generally been guarded with conditions to prevent any permanent injury to Government property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: irrigation water use permitted provided it causes no material damage; temporary connections to post water systems allowed with equitable sharing of operating expenses or limits on beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to dispose of surplus utilities vs. water
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation act gave authority to dispose of surplus ice and electric light and power 'on such terms as prescribed by the Secretary of War' but did not give similar authority to sell surplus water from a post water system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangements such as town supplying fuel and labor to pump water and receiving it through Government system may be lawful as a license to receive water, not a sale of appropriated property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferries and state police power limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has no power to grant or prohibit licenses to establish ferries across navigable waters within a State (police power of the State), but the Secretary of War may give a revocable license for landing at a U.S. pier provided no injury and no exclusive use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landing license requires that landing be made without injury to the pier and not involve exclusive use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to permit temporary use of surplus nonessential military items
rubrics_metrics.description: Where supplies (e.g., musical instruments) are in excess of legitimate demands, the Secretary of War may permit their use by non-official volunteer groups if it promotes welfare and contentment of enlisted men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case-by-case discretion exercised when welfare of troops is advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated permissible temporary licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocable licenses for various temporary uses have been granted under proper regulations: target practice, landing of boats, submarine cable landing, bathing beach, occupying vacant buildings, using unused defenses, temporary telephone offices, storehouses, refuges for fishermen, churches, schoolhouses, life-saving station keepers, stockyards, roads, tramways/temporary railways, electric railway extensions, spur tracks, poles and wires, underground pipes, irrigating ditches, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive examples and citations given demonstrating the variety of permissible, typically non-permanent uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and statutory limits for post office accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail facilities may be regarded as sufficient consideration for placing accommodations at the service of the Post Office Department, but statutory regulations (e.g., lock box rentals) cannot be waived by the Postmaster General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing arrangements to be continued so long as in public interest; applicable statutes control certain matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public easements and state consent where federal fee lacks exclusive jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the United States acquires a reservation subject to the public easement in a highway and not exclusive jurisdiction, control and regulation of that public easement remain with the State; consent of State highway authorities and of the U.S. as fee owner is necessary to impose additional burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary cannot enlarge easement absent statute but may permit location of railway or line under a revocable license that imposes no new easement and is revocable; parties should first obtain state consents.

rubrics_metrics.name: No authority to license premises not owned or controlled by U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War is not empowered to grant a revocable license to use premises not belonging to the United States or not under his control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When U.S. holds only structures (cribs, pilework) and not soil, it cannot grant use interfering with owner's rights without concurrence; owner may be permitted to construct docks if navigation and dike not injured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation and right to remove property
rubrics_metrics.description: A revocable license is an assurance the licensee will not be molested as a trespasser while license remains unrevoked; when revoked, licensee may be required to remove his property without unreasonable delay and should be allowed to remove materials placed under permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include temporary fences and materials left on reservation—licensees permitted to remove them upon revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railroad tracks established by license may be ejected but relocation recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a railroad's track was located upon a reservation by license or sufferance (without congressional right-of-way), the company may be ejected by judicial proceedings; advisable to designate a new location and give notice to move, for which a revocable license may be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice recommends providing new designated location to accommodate command needs and issue a revocable license for the new occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'military stores' and coverage of accountability regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'military stores' in section 1241 R.S. covers property purchased for works of fortification but not civil river and harbor works; however, property accountability regulations cover all property under the Secretary of War's control, including river and harbor property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinction drawn for purposes of section 1241 but accountability rules apply broadly to Department property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1241 R.S. sales require proper inspection and public auction
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sale under section 1241 R.S. (sale of military stores damaged or unsuitable), the property must be inspected and pronounced unsuitable by officers designated by the Secretary of War, and sales shall be made under prescribed regulations (requirement of public auction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations and multiple opinions require formal inspection/survey by designated commissioned officers; certain appraisements and commander certificates may suffice in special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'unsuitable' under section 1241
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Unsuitable' refers to unfitness for use other than that caused by being 'damaged' (e.g., uniform of wrong size); it is not limited to inferior quality and may include items too superior or otherwise unadaptable; not merely excess quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include wrong-sized uniforms; surplus quantity alone does not make stores 'unsuitable' under statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubtful classification of waste/scrap as 'military stores'
rubrics_metrics.description: It is doubtful whether empty barrels, boxes, crates, scrap metals, ground bone, and other waste products accumulating at arsenals constitute 'military stores' requiring inspection and sale procedures under section 1241.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinions differ; an amendment later addressed inspection requirements for some enumerated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber on reservations: general prohibition but exceptions when damaged/unsuitable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no statute authorizing sale of timber on military reservations generally, so Secretary cannot authorize such sales; however, timber that has reached maturity and begun to deteriorate or timber injured (e.g., by tornado) may be regarded as damaged/unsuitable and sold under section 1241.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court/agency rulings allow disposal when inspection finds timber damaged/unsuitable; driftwood with value treated as other property under War Department control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearing timber by contract as incident to sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Where sanitary reasons require clearing reservation timber and underbrush, a contract may be entered providing that timber and underbrush become contractor's property, with proper clearing regarded as incident to sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to lawfully clear and dispose of otherwise unmarketable/unsuitable vegetation under sec 1241 rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales on credit and disposal modes under public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the authority in section 1241, military stores might legally be sold on credit if such a mode of disposition is deemed for the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical practice supports discretionary sale terms when beneficial to public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on paying commissions from sale proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncommissioned officer acting as auctioneer at a public sale of condemned quartermaster stores cannot legally be paid a commission out of sale proceeds; pay and allowances of enlisted men are fixed by law. A civilian employee hired for such services may be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory constraints govern compensation from proceeds; use civilian hire authority where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract settlements vs. sales (returnable barrels example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions where goods were purchased with understanding that empties would be returned at agreed valuation should not be regarded as sales but as contract settlements, so statutory inspection requirements for sales do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization of the transaction (sale vs. contract settlement) determines applicability of section 1241 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of condemned property for experiments or temporary loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Condemned property ordered sold may, in the Secretary's discretion, be loaned or its sale deferred for purposes such as medical experiments or temporary use by an institution; statutory requirements for sale are directory to the extent of vesting sale incidents in Secretary's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include veterinary experiments on condemned animals and loaning a condemned searchlight to a National Home prior to sale.
